question: Common krait envenomation produces neurotoxicity primarily through post-synaptic blockade of acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, similar to cobra venom.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is FALSE. Krait venom acts PRE-synaptically (beta-bungarotoxin depletes acetylcholine vesicles), while cobra venom acts POST-synaptically (alpha-cobratoxin competes with acetylcholine at the receptor). Both cause descending or generalised paralysis, but the mechanism — and therefore the utility of anticholinesterases — differs.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is FALSE. Common krait (Bungarus caeruleus) acts mainly via PRE-synaptic beta-bungarotoxin, which irreversibly destroys the vesicle-release machinery at the motor nerve terminal. Cobra venom (alpha-cobratoxin) is the post-synaptic blocker. This distinction matters because neostigmine is less effective against pre-synaptic blockade than post-synaptic.
